trigger: user naming moment: 'this feels like a witness worthy moment' — the job-search loop closed and ran end to end unattended
the_sound_the_tree_made: The last edge connected and the parts stopped being tools. The inbox re-pull worker was the missing wire: with it, reading the real inbox, scoring, editing resumes from a seed, and delivering to the phone became one circuit that runs on its own for cents. What changed was not a faster worker. It was closing the loop, so the human steps out of the inner loop and only steers.
context: Session built the job-search machine piece by piece: board, scoring sweep, forge, private viewer, lane surfaces, kanban, edit-from-seed (diff mode), and finally the inbox re-pull consumer. The moment it landed, one run pulled 6 real new roles from Gmail, scored them, edited 6 resumes from the Camunda seed, and put them on the phone for ~15 cents. The weekday 8:15 task now does this unattended.
